text:
Randomized Drift Theorem
Reusing a learned procedure through paid local drift probes

Private Astra P3, 23 October 2026. This continues the acquired-representation
work after the negative retaining-U-statistic comparison. The construction is
valid, but its independently chosen algebra fixtures fail the cost test. No
scientific advantage or new general law of intelligence is established.
Historical priority of this exact specialization is UNKNOWN.

The change in question is substantive: acquire a function from experience,
then use it to acquire a new expectation under a changed payoff or changed
dynamics. The old function need not remain accurate for the new estimator to
remain unbiased. Its accuracy and the distribution of local noise determine
whether the operation is worth using. This is a computational use of partial
knowledge, not recognition of an exact model class.

1. The scientific obstruction

A small local equation residual need not imply a small long-time prediction
error. In the chain with one transient state x,

P(x,x)=1-lambda, P(x,B)=lambda*p, P(x,A)=lambda*(1-p),

the eventual B probability is p, while a boundary-correct guess h(x)=c has
local residual lambda*(p-c). The mean absorption time is 1/lambda. Residuals
can be arbitrarily small while the prediction error remains order one.

Furthermore, under local-transition sampling, p=1/4 and p=3/4 produce identical
transcripts until an exit. At most N transition calls leave common no-exit
mass (1-lambda)^N. Uniform testing error <=alpha therefore needs

N >= log(1/(2 alpha))/[-log(1-lambda)].

This is an information obstruction for the specified access model, not a
computational lower bound when the source code exposes the transition row.
An exact committor p does not identify lambda or a deadline probability.

With killed operator K and R=(I-K)^(-1), a learned committor residual r_q gives
error R r_q. If a second learned function approximates the lead-time numerator
w=R q, its error is R r_w + R^2 r_q. The final ratio w/q can contain useful
cancellations, so separate sharp global estimates of both functions may be
an unnecessarily demanding task. These facts are proved in the independent
notes ../external/STOPPED_RESIDUAL_NEXT_MECHANISM.md and
../structure/KILLED_OCCUPATION_VALUE_REUSE.md.

Published short-trajectory learning is already a strong comparator:
Strahan--Finkel--Dinner--Weare (2023), arXiv:2208.01717v2, learns a committor,
adaptively collects further trajectories and reuses its dataset for lead time
in a 75-dimensional atmospheric model. This branch did not execute that model.

2. An operation without an exact conditional-expectation oracle

Fix a finite horizon H and a complete digital Markov state. It must actually
be possible to restore a saved state and generate a fresh one-step transition.
Let T=min(tau,H), where tau is an optional absorbing-boundary time. Retain a
main trajectory X_0,...,X_T. For clarity start at a fixed transient state;
random initial states are permitted if their values are retained in every
formula, and T=0 skips all local probes.

A learned, frozen, bounded program h_t(x) in [0,1] is available. It can be an
ordinary retained regression program. Training, model search, failed attempts
and evaluation costs count. Time or event flags are part of state. The new
target is E G, where G=g(T,X_T) in [0,1] is specified before evaluation.
No agreement between g and h at the boundary is required.

On the retained path write

e_i = h_(i+1)(X_(i+1))-h_i(X_i),
M = sum_i e_i = h_T(X_T)-h_0(X_0),
r_i = E[h_(i+1)(Y)|X_i]-h_i(X_i),
A = sum_i r_i.

The r_i and A are proof quantities, NOT inference inputs. Choose any exactly
sampleable positive probabilities rho_i over the T preterminal positions.
They may inspect the whole retained trajectory. For each of k independent
queries, choose I from rho and draw a fresh Y from the current transition
kernel at X_I, independently conditional on the main path. Return

D = [h_(I+1)(Y)-h_I(X_I)]/rho_I.

The executable estimator is

Q = G-M+(1/k) sum_j D_j.                              (1)

Conditional on the main path, E D=A. Finite stopping and the Markov property
give E M=E A. Hence E Q=E G exactly. There is no call to P h, no normalizer,
no inverse operator and no recognition oracle hidden in (1).

One realization takes T+k transition calls, bounded by H+k. It also retains
T+1 states, evaluates the learned function, constructs and samples rho, and
copies/restores states. Those costs are separate from the transition count.

The reusable validity claim is exact: choose a new kernel and payoff before
fresh evaluation, then generate BOTH main paths and local probes from that
new kernel. The same old h still gives an unbiased estimator. Its former
accuracy certificate is not being transported to the new law. Any variance
or practical advantage must be acquired again or justified separately.

This is not a guarantee for a new payoff chosen after inspecting the same
evaluation outcomes. Such selection needs fresh evaluation or a simultaneous
class guarantee. Fitting h or its regression coefficients on those outcomes
also needs a separate dependence argument.

Precision and randomization

The code uses exact rational h outputs and integer index weights. A learned
floating program can instead be frozen, clipped and deterministically
quantized; that actual executable function is h. No bound on its approximation
to an ideal h is needed for unbiasedness. The values used in the telescoping
term and local probes must be consistent. The divisor rho_I must equal the
actual sampling probability; silently using an approximate divisor can bias
the estimate. Physical and simulator-discretization errors are separate.

Positive probabilities guarantee integrability because
E[|D| | path] <= T. They do NOT guarantee finite variance over arbitrary path
laws. A declared floor rho_i>=eta/T gives |D|<=H/eta. The index sampler uses
exact rejection sampling: actual bits and rejected words are recorded, but
there is no deterministic finite random-bit bound. Expected words per
nontrivial draw are less than two. Integer and score precision also cost work.

3. The equally informed retaining method

The main endpoint G is already paid for. It must remain available. Its observed
increments also provide a free conditional-mean-zero index control:

J = (1/k) sum_j [e_(I_j)/rho_(I_j)-M].                 (2)

For any fixed coefficients beta,gamma, the output

Z = G + beta*(Q-G) - gamma*J                          (3)

is unbiased. An ordinary retaining control-variate learner can fit both
coefficients on independent training. This family contains the proposed Q,
the direct endpoint and the familiar paired-main/side increment control.
Population-optimal coefficients below are deliberately labeled ORACLE
diagnostics: they are not free acquired knowledge.

Stratified local probes are another strong conventional option. With T
queries, one fresh transition at each retained position has conditional
variance sum_i sigma_i^2, where sigma_i^2=Var(h_(i+1)(Y)|X_i). IID uniform
indices with k=T have the additional nonnegative term
sum_i r_i^2-A^2/T. Without-replacement sampling, learned allocation and
conditional Monte Carlo remain eligible comparisons.

4. An exact criterion for whether extra probes can pay

Assume the initial state is transient, so every main path receives k probes,
and the stated finite second moments exist. Define one-probe conditional
quantities, before averaging k replicas:

B = sum_i E[(h_(i+1)(Y)-h_i(X_i))^2 | X_i]/rho_i,
a = Var(A-M),
b = E[B-A^2],
j = E[sum_i e_i^2/rho_i-M^2],
z = E[sum_i r_i*e_i/rho_i-A*M],
c = Cov(G,A-M), V=Var(G), L=E T.

All are proof/audit quantities until learned from paid observations. For
C_0=Q-G, conditional variance decomposition gives

Var(C_0)=a+b/k, Var(J)=j/k, Cov(C_0,J)=z/k,
Cov(G,C_0)=c, Cov(G,J)=0.

If j>0 put d=b-z^2/j; if j=0 put d=b (PSD forces z=0). Residualizing the
index control gives C_0-(z/j)J, with variance a+d/k. Consequently the best
fixed linear use of both controls has variance

V_opt(k) = V-c^2/(a+d/k).                            (4)

Now suppose a>0 and V>0, and define

R = c^2/(V*a),  E = d/a.

Here 0<=R<=1 measures alignment with the new payoff. E measures the remaining
local-probe noise relative to the main martingale energy. These are scalar
descriptions of performance, not assumed representations or oracle inputs.
Equation (4) becomes

V_opt(k) = V [1-R*k/(k+E)].                          (5)

The direct estimator costs L transitions and has variance V. The exact
difference in expected transition cost times variance is

(L+k)V_opt(k)-L V
  = V*k [E-L*R+(1-R)*k]/(k+E).                      (6)

Therefore an improvement is possible at the selected positive k exactly when

E+(1-R)*k < L*R.                                    (7)

In particular E>=LR rules out an advantage for EVERY positive k, even with
oracle coefficients. For integer k>=1 and R<1 the existence condition is
E+1-R<LR. The weaker strict condition E<L*R describes only a positive
continuous interval. When 0<R<1 and that interval exists, the continuous
optimum is

k_star = sqrt[R*E*(L-E)/(1-R)]-E,

subject to k>=1 and integer rounding. R=1 has its limiting optimum as k grows;
R=0 supplies no variance reduction. Actual copying, arithmetic, fitting and
confidence costs can only weaken a transition-only favorable comparison.

A lower bound on the missing information

M-A is the finite stopped martingale sum of h_(i+1)(X_(i+1)) minus its
conditional expectation. Martingale orthogonality gives

a = E sum_i sigma_i^2.

The fresh side-transition noise is orthogonal to J, which depends only on
the main path and the selected index. Thus

d >= E sum_i sigma_i^2/rho_i >= a,

and E>=1 whenever a>0. For uniform rho the first bound is
E >= E[T sum_i sigma_i^2]/E[sum_i sigma_i^2]. Extra noisy local information
does not become free just because h is an accurate program.

This does NOT force E>=L. Concentration of local stochastic energy can in
principle make E much smaller than the average path length. That is the
specific structural opportunity a later acquisition method would need to
obtain and exploit. The present fixtures do not establish it.

There is a useful whole-class obstruction. If sigma_i^2 is the SAME positive
constant at every visited transient position, then Cauchy-Schwarz on rho gives

d >= sigma^2 E[T^2], a=sigma^2 E T,
E >= E[T^2]/E T >= E T=L >= L*R.

No positive k and no positive full-path-dependent index proposal can improve
cost times variance within this IID-index/fixed-control family. The one-state
geometric trap with a time-independent h satisfies this hypothesis (or has
zero control variance, which is already a singular no-gain case). This does
not cover arbitrary time-dependent h, heteroscedastic noise, stratification,
state-dependent sample counts, nonuniform transition costs or stronger access.

Singular cases are harmless. If V=0 the direct endpoint already has zero
variance. If a=0, c=0 and there is no reduction; in the genuine transition
model the remaining quadrature and index controls coincide. If j=0, z=0.
No formula should divide by an uncertified tiny empirical covariance.

5. How performance information can be acquired

Two independent side probes on each retained path give D_1,D_2 and J_1,J_2.
Let C_l=-M+D_l. Then the following paid pilot targets identify the relevant
moments without P h:

a = E[C_1 C_2],
c = E[G C_1],
b = (1/2)E[(D_1-D_2)^2],
j = (1/2)E[(J_1-J_2)^2],
z = (1/2)E[(D_1-D_2)(J_1-J_2)].                      (8)

E C_l=0 is a theorem, not a fitted centering constant. Independent main paths
also provide V=(1/2)E[(G-G')^2] and L=E T. With a global probability floor,
all displayed variables are bounded; ordinary simultaneous concentration
intervals and outward interval arithmetic can provide sufficient performance
tests. The products can have large bounds of order (H/eta)^2. Their precision,
confidence and pilot costs may erase any saving. No inexpensive acquisition
claim is made from (8).

A simpler practical alternative is to freeze candidate coefficients from a
training set, then compare fresh bounded outputs and actual costs directly.
Training, choosing among many candidates and validating a claimed gain must
all be charged. A retaining program learner has the same options.

6. Executable challenge and stronger negative conclusion

The structure-access worker froze three small rational chains before seeing
root code. Root froze the audit before reading their numeric contents. They
are independent algebra challenges, not independently measured scientific
systems and not evidence of learned transfer. The h and rho proposals are
supplied fixture values; no training acquisition is being concealed.

The exact audit passed 1,799 checks, covering all 37 stopped main paths across
the three original cases, direct one- and two-probe moment expansion,
fixed mixtures, modified payoffs and swapped exit laws. The latter are
exploratory algebra checks. Forty-eight frozen executable demonstrations
used 243 actual source transitions, 622 source-random bits and 311 index bits;
all transitions, rejected random words and outputs are retained and replayed.

After that result, the general cost criterion (6) was derived and independently
checked. This is a disclosed post-test analytical strengthening, with no new
source samples or retuning. For the three fixed h/rho proposals:

Independent fixture	R	E	L*R	Conclusion
Geometric trap, imperfect h	0.978773	3.888604	2.986021	No k>0 improvement
Branching and unequal traps	0.992701	3.206922	2.729927	No k>0 improvement
Alternating residuals	0.967843	5.323566	2.464974	No k>0 improvement

The comparison is unusually favorable to the proposed method: it supplies
the exact best fixed regression coefficients without charging their learning.
Despite strong alignment R, irreducible/index probe noise removes the benefit.
Adding fitting and verification costs cannot repair that loss. The theorem
does not exclude a different h, different allocation, stratification, stronger
source access or another scientific system.

Because these transition tables are explicitly available, a truly equally
informed method could also solve their small finite-horizon equations exactly.
The results challenge algebra and cost claims; they are not a black-box speed
benchmark. More authored or larger versions would not resolve the scientific
question, and this benchmark is not being prolonged.

7. Prior and the next scientific distinction

Henderson--Glynn (2002) already develops approximate-value martingale controls.
Munos (2006), Theorem 2 and Remark 3, supplies an especially strong cumulative
learning precedent: learned representations can progressively reduce variance,
but evaluating the operator-applied representation is substantive. Remark 3
explicitly warns that substituting a realized next state can erase the gain
and suggests learning P phi_j. Wang--Blanchet--Glynn (2024) and
Gupta--Khammash (2014) already randomize sparse auxiliary work in generator-based
sensitivity calculations. Those source contracts differ from (1); absence of
an exact formula in this bounded search does not establish novelty.

The next discriminating object is therefore an acquired library carrying
useful approximations to BOTH phi_j and their pushed-forward responses
P phi_j, or an acquired local-variance allocation with a paid confidence
warrant. A new experiment must show that obtaining this extra machinery makes
a subsequent scientific task cheaper after training, coverage, precision and
validation are counted. The equally informed baseline is retained
Feynman--Kac/Galerkin learning with operator approximation, stratified local
probes, and generator/innovation controls whenever the simulator exposes them.
No exact conditional-expectation oracle may be assumed for either method.

The immediate stronger construction is explicit. Given a paid learned drift
proxy m_i for r_i, replace the drift estimate by

A_hat = sum_i m_i
        + (1/k) sum_j [h_(I_j+1)(Y_j)-h_(I_j)(X_(I_j))-m_(I_j)]/rho_(I_j).

Its conditional mean is still A. Its conditional variance times k is

sum_i [sigma_i^2+(r_i-m_i)^2]/rho_i
  - [sum_i(r_i-m_i)]^2.

Thus learning m can remove index variation in the drift but cannot remove
the independent-child term sum_i sigma_i^2/rho_i. Learning a corresponding
variance allocation has a separate acquisition cost. This identity specifies
the exact next implementation and measurement target; it is not a tested
advantage, and ordinary retaining learners that learn P phi_j get this same
construction. The next empirical test must distinguish heterogeneity of
obtainable local stochastic energy from a supplied decomposition.

This is a specific unresolved acquisition problem, not a claim that cumulative
learning is impossible. The acquired subspace, signed residual sampling,
circuit/composition results, network bounds and their negative comparisons
remain preserved unchanged.

Exact artifacts: randomized_drift_quadrature.py; audit_randomized_drift.py;
DRIFT_QUADRATURE_AUDIT_CONTRACT.json; DRIFT_QUADRATURE_AUDIT_RESULT.json;
DRIFT_QUADRATURE_ACTUAL_TAPES.json; DRIFT_ALL_PROBE_COST_RESULT.json.

Training, choosing among many candidates and validating a claimed gain must
all be charged. A retaining program learner has the same options.

7. Prior and the next scientific distinction

Henderson--Glynn (2002) already develops approximate-value martingale controls.
Munos (2006), Theorem 2 and Remark 3, supplies an especially strong cumulative
learning precedent: learned representations can progressively reduce variance,
but evaluating the operator-applied representation is substantive. Remark 3
explicitly warns that substituting a realized next state can erase the gain
and suggests learning P phi_j. Wang--Blanchet--Glynn (2024) and
Gupta--Khammash (2014) already randomize sparse auxiliary work in generator-based
sensitivity calculations. Those source contracts differ from (1); absence of
an exact formula in this bounded search does not establish novelty.

The next discriminating object is therefore an acquired library carrying
useful approximations to BOTH phi_j and their pushed-forward responses
P phi_j, or an acquired local-variance allocation with a paid confidence
warrant. A new experiment must show that obtaining this extra machinery makes
a subsequent scientific task cheaper after training, coverage, precision and
validation are counted. The equally informed baseline is retained
Feynman--Kac/Galerkin learning with operator approximation, stratified local
probes, and generator/innovation controls whenever the simulator exposes them.
No exact conditional-expectation oracle may be assumed for either method.

The immediate stronger construction is explicit. Given a paid learned drift
proxy m_i for r_i, replace the drift estimate by

A_hat = sum_i m_i + (1/k) sum_j [h_(I_j+1)(Y_j)-h_(I_j)(X_(I_j))-m_(I_j)]/rho_(I_j).

Its conditional mean is still A. Its conditional variance times k is

sum_i [sigma_i^2+(r_i-m_i)^2]/rho_i - [sum_i(r_i-m_i)]^2.

Thus learning m can remove index variation in the drift but cannot remove
the independent-child term sum_i sigma_i^2/rho_i. Learning a corresponding
variance allocation has a separate acquisition cost. This identity specifies
the exact next implementation and measurement target; it is not a tested
advantage, and ordinary retaining learners that learn P phi_j get this same
construction. The next empirical test must distinguish heterogeneity of
obtainable local stochastic energy from a supplied decomposition.

This is a specific unresolved acquisition problem, not a claim that cumulative
learning is impossible. The acquired subspace, signed residual sampling,
circuit/composition results, network bounds and their negative comparisons
remain preserved unchanged.
